verdict.rationale: Basecamp's own features give a kind of status tracking: Hill Charts show 'where things really stand', and card tables track work through 'distinct stages'. Work can be assigned to people. There is no evidence of initiative-level tracking with an explicit priority field or a designated owning team. Missing for 10: a priority attribute, team ownership of initiatives (assignment is per item, not per team), an initiative/portfolio-level object distinct from projects, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a product manager, I can track initiatives with status, priority, and an owning team

citations.quote: Basecamp’s Hill Charts let you know exactly where things really stand.
Perfect for bug and issue tracking, software development, production work, or anything with distinct stages.
Assign items, set due dates, attach files, even create subtasks.
